excerpts.author: .christn
excerpts.content:
Yes, we do. 
In your case, the fact that your requests are getting routed across the atlantic lead to an underestimation of the return latency in certain cases. 
I added another 150ms of buffer so responses should reach you in time now.

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: so if a client doesn't sent these, do you reject the request? need to make sure all clients actually sent this as it was previously handled by the sidecar

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Oh interesting I wonder what's the limit this can be pushed, getting an early attestation deadline is the ultimate goal to remove useless part of the slot

excerpts.author: .christn
excerpts.content: No we don't reject the request. We use a fallback algorithm / heuristic to estimate the deadline and delay based on that.

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: per gloas spec these headers are required now, so while your heuristic is fine, it shouldn't be required, but need to find clients that are non spec compliant during ideally during devnet testing
